3. The defendant’s case is that the suit is not maintainable and this Court has go, no jurisdiction to adjudicate upon the plaintiff's claim; the suit is bad for misjoinder and non-joinder of parties; and that the suit is barred by limitation. According to the defendant the vessel arrived on 29.7.80 at Chittagong Outer Anchorage with 3,400 metric tons of cement and 540 tons of tallow belonged to another party. The vessel could not take berth as there was no berthing space at the Port. It finally took berth at the Jetty on 10.8.80 for discharging the cargo belonging to the defendant and another. She discharged 1355 metric tons of cement and 340 tons of tallow in the first placement and being unable to discharge the entire cargo at the safe berth was ordered by the Port to leave the Jetty and accordingly the vessel left the Jetty. The defendant's case is that as per liner terms the plaintiff could unload the cargo without waiting for the consignee: and that their agent bad already realised the cost of transportation and handling charge from the consignee as per approved rates of the Port and that the owner of the ship cannot compel the consignee to receive the cargo imported on the liner freight, direct i.e. from the ship hook; rather the consignee has the option to receive the cargo from the ship-hook or at the jetty shed en payment of space lent if required. According to the defendant, she took necessary steps through its agent to help the plaintiff in discharging the goods. The defendant's case is that the defendants not liable to take steps for delivery of the cargo and as such the alleged causing of unnecessary detention of the vessel for 22 days does not arise and the defendant is not liable to pay for the alleged demurrage and incidental expenses; that there is no clause or condition for damage for the detention of the vessel in the Bill of Lading; and that as per clause 8 to Charter party agreement the owners of the ship have a lien on the cargo and the Charterers are responsible for the alleged damage for the detention, if any. 

 5. The plaintiff has examined only one witness, P W. 1 the Shipping Manager of M/S Aquatic Shipping Ltd. the local agent of the plaintiff M/S. Eastern Steamship Private Ltd. has given the plaint case. The ship arrived on 29th July, 1980 and left Bangladesh on 30th August, 1980. She brought a cargo of 4,000 metric tons out of which 3,400 tons of cement belonged to the defendant. The Plaintiff notified by advertisement in the Bangladesh Times on 26.7.80 about the arrival of the ship and also sent a letter to the defendant on 1.8.80. The defendant was informed that for non-receipt of the cargo it would be liable to pay detention charges at the rate of US dollar 600/- per day. By another letter dated 5th August, 1980 the defendant was again informed. Similar letters were sent on 16-8-80, 21-8-80 and 24-8-80. The plaintiff also sent several telegrams on l8th, 19th and 27th August, 1980 to the defendant. By a letter dated 11-8-80 the plaintiff applied to the Jetty authorities for giving permission to discharge 2,000 tons of cement at the jetty shed since the consignees were not ready to take delivery of their cargo. The plaintiff sent a letter on 3-9-80 claiming damage for the detention. Their solicitors sent a similar demand on 16-9-80. P. W. 1 stales that according to his calculation the vessel was detained for about 22 days since normally about 750 metric tons of cement can be discharged per day. This witness also states in examination in chief that the owners did not exercise the lien of the cargo and that the freight was prepaid, and the cargo was brought under liner terms and the owners were responsible to discharge the cargo to the consignees at the owners costs and risks, and if the consignees fail to come forward to take delivery of the cargo it is the owners option to discharge the same at the jetty. P. W. 1 states that be has claimed damages at the instructions of their principal.
